reason: Prior n=512 measurements show no promotion for panel calls, traversal changes, padding, transpose wrappers, or loop scheduling; noisy scores do not identify a cache cause. I rank the distinct smaller A-panel layout first because it targets the measured path and may reduce its active scratch footprint, while treating that benefit as unverified. Fusing transpose with compute could remove scratch traffic, but its repeated register transposes raise correctness and performance risk. One-level Strassen is approved and saves arithmetic by count, but timed copies, recombination, seven calls, and FP32 error risk are substantial. The two Strassen workspace proposals overlap; test the bounded schedule before its allocation-only variation. Assembly audit ranks low because the supplied evidence already questions legal post-index loads with unequal strides. The remaining proposals affect general sizes or perform a mapping/schedule permutation with no evidence of n=512 benefit.
